title: Medicaid Allowed Ratio Valuation of Plan Appeals — Insurance Coverage & Claims
content:
**Insurance Coverage & Claims, Medicaid Managed Care Plan — valuation of plan appeals.**

**Medicaid allowed ratio.** A Medicaid allowed ratio is the plan's payment plus the member responsibility it assigned, divided by that payment plus the contractual adjustment plus that member responsibility. The *claim's own ratio* takes these amounts over the claim's lines; the *coverage's twelve-month ratio* takes them over every such line on the coverage within the last twelve months.

**Valuation ratio.** The plan appeal's valuation ratio is the claim's own Medicaid allowed ratio where the plan paid at least one line of the claim; it is the coverage's twelve-month ratio where no line of the claim was paid but the coverage carries a plan payment within the last twelve months; otherwise it is one. Under the plan appeal, the disputed charges are multiplied by the valuation ratio.

## Conditions and outcomes

| Plan paid a line of the claim | Plan payment on the coverage within twelve months | Ratio used |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | — | Claim's own Medicaid allowed ratio |
| No | Yes | Coverage's twelve-month Medicaid allowed ratio |
| No | No | One (billed value) |

## Hypothetical case

No line of the appealed claim was paid. Over the last twelve months the coverage shows plan payments of 540.00 USD, contractual adjustments of 420.00 USD and member responsibility of 40.00 USD. The twelve-month ratio is 540.00 plus 40.00, 580.00, divided by 540.00 plus 420.00 plus 40.00, 1000.00: 0.58. Disputed charges of 250.00 USD multiplied by 0.58 give 145.00 USD.
